evidence.creator: shankar s.
evidence.description: We then took a taxi back into downtown Davao, to the San Pedro shopping street. San Pedro St. is considered to be the oldest street in Davao city. Unfortunately, thanks to a just concluded feverish election campaign, the local politicos had promised to make up for their excesses by saving power. Due to tis, much of the street lighting had been switched off and we had to rely on the lights from the many hand cards, many of which were unlit anyway. Frankly, had it not been for my delightful travel companions, I might never have ventured into that street in the dark. The recently stopped rain made things darker still. Here is an overview of the shopping area with greatly curtailed street lighting. Structure seen here is the Rizal Park stage on San Pedro in Davao. Love the fabulous metal eagle motif atop the shed.  (Davao, Philippines, May 2013)

evidence.description: Baker's Hill also starting point of the 'zip line' where you hook yourself to a cable and rocket across a deep valley to the other side. A true adrenaline rush if there was one, as your life literally hands by a single thread! I'll pass this one on, thank you very much. The hut you see in the foreground is the starting point for the zipline. Incidentally, Filpinos obviously love their ziplines, I found several of these rides in Davao, Cebu, two in Bohol, and here in Puerto Princesa. In Cebu, the zipline was across tall buildings. In the horizon is the Puerto Princesa bay. (Puerto Princesa, Philippines, May 2013)
